finding.claim: SCP directory download lets a malicious SCP server write files outside the destination directory: an E record received before any D decrements directoryCounter to -1, the exit check only tests == 0, and the parent-directory walk at lines 908-912 keeps moving up, so later C records create or overwrite files in ancestor directories (up to filesystem root). EnsureValidLocalName only validates the filename, not the directory.
finding.source: Server-sent SCP protocol messages on the scp -prf exec channel, read in ScpClient.Download(string, DirectoryInfo) at ScpClient.cs:520-546 and passed to InternalDownload at ScpClient.cs:884-895
finding.sink: new FileInfo(Path.Combine(currentDirectoryFullName, fileName)) and fileInfo.Open(FileMode.Create) at ScpClient.cs:963-966

trace.note: Public Download(string, DirectoryInfo) calls InternalDownload(channel, input, directoryInfo)
ReadString(input) reads an attacker-controlled protocol message
directoryCounter-- on E takes 0 to -1 when no D was received
Exit check is only directoryCounter == 0, so -1 never breaks the loop
Parent of currentDirectoryFullName is taken; Debug.Assert at 910 is a no-op in release builds
currentDirectoryFullName is moved up one level; repeated E messages walk to root
EnsureValidLocalName(fileName) rejects separators, '.', '..', empty names; the directory is not checked
File path is combined with the walked-up directory
FileMode.Create truncates and overwrites an existing file in the ancestor directory

finding.guards_checked: EnsureValidLocalName (ScpClient.cs:840-854) validates the filename only. The == 0 exit check (ScpClient.cs:903) does not reject negative counters. Root-null handling is only Debug.Assert (ScpClient.cs:910), after which the null dereference at 912 aborts the loop. No check constrains currentDirectoryFullName to remain under the start directory.

finding.claim: The default SCP remote-path transform only escapes double quotes and does not escape backslash, dollar sign, or backtick, so a caller-supplied remote path containing $(...), backticks, or a backslash before a quote runs arbitrary commands on the SSH server through the scp exec request.
finding.source: Caller-supplied remote path string (for example a user-influenced file name) passed to ScpClient upload/download methods that use the default constructor transform
finding.sink: channel.SendExecRequest with scp command containing the transformed path, at ScpClient.cs:367, 410, 459, 498, 538, 578

trace.note: Public constructors without an explicit transform, e.g. lines 267-298, pass DefaultTransform
Only '"' is escaped; '\\', '$', and backtick are appended unchanged
Result is wrapped in double quotes and returned
Transformed path is interpolated into the scp -prf exec command string sent to the remote shell

finding.guards_checked: The only control is the quote-escaping loop at RemotePathDoubleQuoteTransformation.cs:57-67, which is incomplete. ShellQuote transform (RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation.cs) is not the default and was checked as sound. No input validation exists on the path in ScpClient.

finding.claim: Host key trust is fail-open by default: CanTrustHostKey returns true when no HostKeyReceived handler is attached, and HostKeyEventArgs initializes CanTrust to true, so a handler that does not explicitly set CanTrust=false accepts any host key. This is a design-level default that weakens server authentication and enables MITM against clients that do not register a verifier.
finding.source: Network attacker positioned between client and SSH server presenting its own host key and valid signature
finding.sink: Host key trust decision in ValidateExchangeHash at KeyExchange.cs:493 (keyAlgorithm.VerifySignature && CanTrustHostKey)

trace.note: No HostKeyReceived handler means return true
CanTrust initialized to true in the constructor path

finding.guards_checked: Signature over the exchange hash is verified (KeyExchange.cs:493). No default verifier is registered in Session.cs or BaseClient.cs (BaseClient.cs:418 only forwards the event). Caveat: this may be the documented contract requiring callers to handle HostKeyReceived; not verified against docs.
